Explanation: The Product Listing is the unit of value made discoverable through Walmart Marketplace: a seller's offer combining the product, price, availability, delivery promise and other information a Shopper uses to decide whether to buy.
Walmart Inc. owns the marketplace environment and its marketplace team governs how third-party Sellers and supporting services participate.
Walmart's job is to expand marketplace assortment and transaction volume while maintaining the customer experience and economics of the broader Walmart ecosystem.
Marketplace growth can expand assortment and customer loyalty while adding referral-fee, advertising and service revenue opportunities without Walmart owning every item sold.
Rapid seller growth can create quality, counterfeit, compliance, customer-service and technology-scaling problems that may damage trust in the Walmart brand.

Walmart sits inside the marketplace transaction: it collects customer payment, deducts category-based referral fees and coordinates settlement or payout to Sellers, while also monetizing services such as advertising.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Order / Pay — Shoppers place marketplace orders and pay through Walmart's checkout. | → Provider · Payout — Walmart coordinates seller settlement after the marketplace transaction, net of applicable fees and adjustments. | ← Provider · Commission — Sellers pay Walmart category-based referral fees on completed marketplace sales. | → Partner · Fees / Contract — Walmart can contract and pay external service partners for logistics, technology, payments, advertising or other marketplace capabilities.

Explanation: Walmart governs entry and participation through product policies, business verification, seller performance standards, reviews, compliance controls, dispute processes and enforcement.
Walmart can promote marketplace demand through its website, app, search visibility, advertising, email, social channels and physical store presence.
Walmart recruits and onboards Sellers, monitors quality and performance, promotes listings and marketplace services, coordinates transactions and scales the platform infrastructure.
The marketplace draws on Walmart's brand, digital platform, commerce data, seller support, marketing reach, legal and policy capabilities, payment infrastructure and physical retail network.
Price-conscious shoppers, families and online buyers use Walmart Marketplace to compare and purchase products from Walmart and third-party Sellers through one customer experience.
Shoppers use the marketplace to find products that meet their needs at competitive prices without having to search across many separate retailers.
A wider assortment, competitive prices, convenience and the Walmart brand can reduce the effort and perceived risk of online shopping.
High prices, weak selection, delivery problems or uncertainty about third-party seller quality can reduce the value of the marketplace for Shoppers.
Shoppers place an order and pay through Walmart's checkout even when the underlying product is offered by a third-party Seller.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Order / Pay — Shoppers place marketplace orders and pay through Walmart's checkout. | ← Provider · Product — The Seller provides the product that fulfills the Shopper's marketplace purchase, directly or through a fulfillment service. | ← Partner · Service — Service Partners can support the Shopper-facing transaction through delivery, payments or other enabling services.

Explanation: Participation can be constrained by account rules, fraud controls, age or product restrictions and the ability to use Walmart's digital channels.
Shoppers reach the marketplace primarily through Walmart.com and the Walmart app, while Walmart's physical stores can support pickup, returns and other parts of the experience.
Shoppers search and compare listings, place orders, pay, receive or pick up purchases and can leave reviews that feed back into marketplace trust.
Shoppers contribute attention, purchase intent, account and payment information, device access and the behavioral data created through their marketplace activity.
Third-party sellers, small businesses and brands supply additional assortment to Walmart Marketplace without Walmart owning that inventory.
Sellers join Walmart Marketplace to reach Walmart's customer base without having to build an equivalent consumer marketplace themselves.
Marketplace participation can provide additional demand, brand exposure, sales scale and performance data while giving Sellers access to Walmart's commerce infrastructure.
Sellers compete for visibility and price while also managing inventory, fulfillment, returns, customer service and marketplace performance requirements.
Sellers supply products to Shoppers through Walmart Marketplace and pay Walmart referral fees on completed sales; fee rates vary by category.
Transaction Flows: ← Owner · Payout — Walmart coordinates seller settlement after the marketplace transaction, net of applicable fees and adjustments. | → Owner · Commission — Sellers pay Walmart category-based referral fees on completed marketplace sales. | → Consumer · Product — The Seller provides the product that fulfills the Shopper's marketplace purchase, directly or through a fulfillment service.

Explanation: Walmart requires business verification, compliant products, marketplace or e-commerce experience, valid product identifiers, returns capability and adherence to seller performance standards.
Sellers manage the marketplace through Seller Center, direct APIs or approved solution providers, depending on their technical setup.
Sellers create and optimize listings, manage price and inventory, fulfill orders directly or through Walmart services, handle support and maintain marketplace performance.
Sellers contribute product data, inventory, pricing, fulfillment capability, seller credentials and the operational capacity required to serve Walmart customers.
Logistics firms, advertising and technology providers, payment services and other solution partners extend capabilities that Walmart or Sellers can use around the marketplace transaction.
Service Partners help make marketplace transactions work at scale through fulfillment, integrations, payments, advertising and other specialist services.
A large marketplace can generate recurring demand, transaction volume, customer reach and revenue opportunities for external service providers.
Service Partners have to cope with technical integration, demand peaks, quality expectations and the operational requirements of participating in Walmart's ecosystem.
Partners provide logistics, technology, payment or advertising services and receive commercial compensation through their contracts or service relationships.
Transaction Flows: ← Owner · Fees / Contract — Walmart can contract and pay external service partners for logistics, technology, payments, advertising or other marketplace capabilities. | → Consumer · Service — Service Partners can support the Shopper-facing transaction through delivery, payments or other enabling services.

Explanation: Partners must meet Walmart's technical, operational and quality requirements; services that cannot scale or meet compliance expectations can lose access.
Service Partners typically connect through APIs, direct business integrations, contractual relationships and operational dashboards rather than the shopper-facing marketplace interface.
Partners integrate their systems, deliver services, maintain service quality and scale capacity as marketplace transaction volume changes.
Partners contribute logistics infrastructure, software and data interfaces, specialist teams and service-level commitments.
